subject: Combine 4 stacks - Error in (function (...)  : Name mismatch.

messages.author: 6824aa3731b12a8f
messages.subject: Combine 4 stacks - Error in (function (...)  : Name mismatch.
parts:
Hi all,

I am fitting a preferential model and so I have to have one stack for the marks likelihood and another for the point process and I want to make predictions of  the marks and of the latent field. However, when I tried to combine the four stacks I had this error 

> Error in (function (...)  : Name mismatch.

I discovered that the error occur when I add the stack for the prediction of the marks (stack.pr). Below are my stacks.

stack.obs<-inla.stack(data=list(y=cbind(y,NA),e=rep(0,n)),
                      A=list(obs,1),
                      effects=list(spatial.field=s.index$spatial.field,
                                   list(data.frame(b0.y=rep(1,n)))),
                      tag="response")
stack.pp<-inla.stack(data=list(y=cbind(NA,ypp),e=epp),
                     A=list(App,1),
                     effects=list(i=s.index$spatial.field,
                                  list(data.frame(b0.pp=rep(1,nv+n),depth=depth.point))),
                     tag="pp")
stack.pr<-inla.stack(data=list(y=NA),
                   A=list(Ap),
                   effects=list(c(s.index,list(b0.y=1))),
                   tag="pred.response")
stack.pred<-inla.stack(data=list(xi=NA),
                       A=list(Ap),
                       effects=list(s.index),
                       tag="pred.latent")

join.stack<-inla.stack(stack.obs,stack.pp,stack.pr,stack.pred)

Can anyone help me?

Thanks in advance,
Lídia

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Combine 4 stacks - Error in (function (...) : Name mismatch.
parts:
Ok, that seems clear;

I think you can just leave out the all-NA y entirely, just as you did for the following stack that only has xi in the data list.

Alternatively, make that y into a two-column NA matrix with the same number of rows as the A-matrices in its stack.

Finn
